title: Waterproofing & Protective Coatings | North Central FL
description: Waterproofing coatings for walls, balconies, and foundations in Gainesville, Ocala, and North Central Florida. Joint detailing, elastomerics, and sealers.
h1: Waterproofing and Protective Coatings for Florida Buildings
heroIntro: We stop water at the joints, penetrations, and edges where it actually gets in, then apply elastomeric wall systems, penetrating sealers, and walking-deck coatings at the specified thickness.
card: Elastomeric wall systems, masonry sealers, and balcony coatings with joint and penetration detailing.

questions: Will waterproof paint stop my wall from leaking?
What is the difference between a sealer and an elastomeric coating?
How do you waterproof a balcony or walking deck?

body: Regular exterior paint sheds normal rain. It is not designed to keep wind-driven water out of a cracked block wall, a second-floor balcony over living space, or a foundation wall that stays damp. When you see interior stains after storms, blistering coatings, or efflorescence blooming on block, you need an exterior waterproofing coating system rather than another coat of house paint.

In North Central Florida the problem is often sideways rain. Summer storms push water horizontally into joints and around windows that would shed a gentle vertical shower without trouble. That is why our first step is figuring out where water is getting in, not picking a product.
Typical clients include homeowners with damp block walls, condo associations with balcony leaks, and commercial owners whose lower walls wick water after every storm.

Wide open fields of wall rarely leak on their own. Water finds its way in at transitions and holes. On the walkthrough the crew lead checks these first, takes moisture readings, and photographs what is found:

Sometimes the cause is hiding behind a finish rather than on it. Wood-framed walls with siding can hold water for a long time before any sign shows inside; our article on hidden moisture damage behind siding explains what to look for. Once the entry points are known, the repair plan and the coating choice become straightforward, and the estimate lists each detail so you can see exactly what is being sealed.
bullets: Control joints and cold joints in block and concrete
Window and door perimeters, sills, and head flashing
Railing posts, light fixtures, hose bibs, and pipe penetrations
Roof-to-wall intersections and missing kickout flashing
Terminations where an old coating simply stops

body: Before field coating, the details are treated. Joints and cracks are routed and filled with a compatible flexible sealant, and transitions that move get reinforcing fabric embedded in the coating. Then the wall itself is coated.

An elastomeric wall coating is a thick, rubbery film that stretches over hairline cracks and blocks liquid water. It goes on much heavier than paint, so we check wet-film thickness with a gauge as we work to make sure the manufacturer's specification is actually met. Elastomerics are ideal on stucco and block with movement; see our stucco repair and painting page for how crack repair fits in.

On brick, natural stone, and architectural concrete where you want to keep the look of the masonry, a clear penetrating water repellent is often the better choice. It soaks in, lines the pores, and causes water to bead without forming a film. It does not bridge cracks, so it only suits sound masonry. Painted block that needs color as well as protection is covered under concrete and masonry painting.

Concrete balconies and breezeways on condos and multi-family buildings take foot traffic, standing water, and full sun. They need a traffic-rated, multi-layer deck coating: a primer, a flexible waterproof base membrane, and a textured wear coat for slip resistance. Cracks and the joint where the slab meets the wall are detailed before the membrane goes down.

For associations and property managers, balcony coatings are often phased with a community repaint. Our HOA and property management painting page explains how phased work and resident notices are handled.

Deck coatings also need upkeep. The textured wear layer gradually thins in high-traffic paths, and periodically adding a fresh topcoat before the membrane is exposed keeps the system working far longer than letting it wear through.

Waterproofing only works if the source is addressed. If water is coming from a missing flashing, a failed roof transition, or an irrigation head blasting the wall, we will say so and recommend fixing that first, rather than coating over a problem that will come back. Wood decks are a different material entirely, handled through deck and fence staining with penetrating stains.

Coating work is scheduled in dry weather, with October through May the most reliable window. Your written estimate names each product, the thickness or number of coats, the detailing steps, and the areas included and excluded. Exterior work carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. Waterproofing is one of our specialty coating services.

faqs.q: Will a waterproof coating stop my wall leak?
faqs.a: If the water is coming through the wall surface or its joints, the right system usually will. If it is coming from flashing, a roof, or plumbing, that source has to be fixed first. We check before recommending a coating.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a sealer and an elastomeric?
faqs.a: A penetrating sealer soaks into masonry and repels water without changing its look, but does not bridge cracks. An elastomeric is a thick flexible film that bridges hairline cracks and adds color.

faqs.q: Can you coat a balcony that people walk on?
faqs.a: Yes, with a traffic-rated deck coating system that includes a waterproof membrane and a textured wear layer for grip.

faqs.q: How do you make sure the coating is thick enough?
faqs.a: We measure wet-film thickness during application and follow the manufacturer's coverage rate, because a thin elastomeric loses most of its crack-bridging ability.
